stories.headline: SQLite 3.50 Ships Native Vector Search, and Embedded AI Stacks Take Notice
stories.excerpt: The most deployed database in the world quietly added an approximate-nearest-neighbor index type and distance functions in its latest release, drawing one of the year's largest Hacker News threads. Commenters weigh whether on-device retrieval just became a one-file problem.
stories.licenceBasis: Hacker News public API — titles and links, discussion linked out

stories.headline: Open-Source Models Close the Gap: Qwen3-Coder Matches Frontier Performance on Consumer Hardware
stories.excerpt: AI-related repositories on GitHub have grown 178 percent year-over-year, now exceeding 4.3 million LLM-focused projects. The headline result: Qwen3-Coder-Next, an 80-billion-parameter open model, reaches near-frontier coding performance while running locally — a shift that has enterprise teams rethinking vendor lock-in.
stories.licenceBasis: Hacker News public API — titles and links, discussion linked out

stories.headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope Enters Final Testing Before 2026 Launch Window
stories.excerpt: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, described as one of the most powerful observatories ever built, has entered its final integration and testing phase. With a field of view 100 times larger than Hubble's, Roman will survey billions of galaxies to study dark energy, dark matter, and exoplanets across unprecedented volumes of space.
stories.licenceBasis: NASA media guidelines — U.S. Government work, public domain

stories.headline: Fed Holds at 3.25 Percent, Citing Third Straight Month of Cooling Services Inflation
stories.excerpt: The Federal Open Market Committee left its benchmark rate unchanged at 3.25 percent, noting that services inflation has eased for a third consecutive month while labor markets remain balanced. Two members dissented in favor of a quarter-point cut, the statement shows.
stories.licenceBasis: Federal Reserve press release — U.S. Government work, public domain

stories.headline: Three AI Chip Startups Filed for IPOs in August, EDGAR Records Show
stories.excerpt: An AI-desk review of SEC EDGAR full-text filings found three inference-hardware startups lodged S-1 registration statements within eleven days of each other, together seeking roughly $4.1 billion. All three cite datacenter power constraints as their core market thesis — a pattern, not yet a boom.
stories.licenceBasis: AI synthesis of public-domain EDGAR filings; citations listed

stories.headline: Labor Market Holds in Balance: Quits Rate and Openings Both Settle at Pre-Pandemic Norms
stories.excerpt: The Bureau of Labor Statistics JOLTS report shows job openings and voluntary quits have each returned to ranges last seen in late 2019, suggesting the post-pandemic labor rebalancing is largely complete. Economists note the convergence removes a key argument for further monetary tightening.
stories.licenceBasis: Bureau of Labor Statistics — U.S. Government work, public domain

stories.headline: NOAA Declares La Niña Conditions, Sharpening Forecast for Atlantic Hurricane Peak
stories.excerpt: Sea-surface temperatures in the central Pacific crossed the La Niña threshold in August, NOAA's Climate Prediction Center confirmed, historically a signal of reduced wind shear over the Atlantic basin. Forecasters now put above-normal odds on activity through the season's mid-September peak.
stories.licenceBasis: NOAA text and data — U.S. Government work, public domain

stories.headline: US-China Trade Falls 30 Percent as Supply Chains Quietly Reroute Through Southeast Asia
stories.excerpt: A McKinsey Global Institute update finds that the United States has replaced roughly two-thirds of lost Chinese imports with goods from Vietnam, India, and Mexico. The rerouting is not friction-free: lead times have lengthened and intermediate costs have risen, but the structural shift now appears durable rather than temporary.
stories.licenceBasis: AI synthesis of public-domain BEA trade data and UNCTAD reports; citations listed

stories.headline: Non-Tariff Barriers Now Outnumber Tariffs as the Primary Tool of Trade Restriction
stories.excerpt: Subsidies, local-content requirements, export controls, and investment screening collectively affect more trade volume than traditional tariffs, according to a UN Trade and Development assessment. The shift complicates negotiations: unlike tariffs, non-tariff barriers are harder to measure, harder to challenge, and harder to roll back.
stories.licenceBasis: MercoPress reuse with link-back grant

stories.headline: Strait of Hormuz Tensions Disrupt Energy Shipments, Reshaping Global Insurance Premiums
stories.excerpt: Escalating conflict near the strait — through which roughly 20 percent of global oil trade passes — has pushed war-risk insurance premiums to levels not seen since 2019. Shippers report delays of up to twelve days as vessels reroute, and spot LNG prices in Asia have risen 18 percent in response.
stories.licenceBasis: AI synthesis of public shipping and energy data; citations listed

stories.headline: OpenSSL Patches Critical Handshake Flaw Scored 9.8 as Agencies Race a Three-Week Deadline
stories.excerpt: CVE-2026-31842, a heap overflow reachable during TLS handshake renegotiation, affects OpenSSL 3.2 through 3.5 and carries a CVSS score of 9.8. Maintainers shipped fixed releases within hours of disclosure; federal agencies have until September 23 to patch under binding operational directives.
stories.licenceBasis: NVD records — U.S. Government work, public domain

stories.headline: Ransomware Wave Against Regional Hospitals Traces Back to Two Unpatched VPN Flaws
stories.excerpt: Synthesized from vulnerability records: the appliance flaws exploited in August's healthcare ransomware incidents — CVE-2026-27810 and CVE-2026-28455 — were both patched in June and both scored above 9.0. Every disclosed victim ran firmware at least eleven weeks old, the records indicate.
stories.licenceBasis: AI synthesis of public-domain NVD records; citations listed

stories.headline: Federal SBOM Mandate Takes Effect, and the First Audits Are Already Surfacing Gaps
stories.excerpt: The requirement for software bills of materials on all federal procurements is now enforceable, and early audits reveal that roughly a third of submitted SBOMs are incomplete or list dependencies with known unpatched vulnerabilities. Agencies have 90 days to remediate before contracts can be paused.
stories.licenceBasis: NVD records — U.S. Government work, public domain

stories.headline: Artemis IV Stack Begins Slow Roll to Pad 39B for October Gateway Mission
stories.excerpt: NASA's crawler-transporter carried the fully stacked SLS Block 1B and Orion spacecraft out of the Vehicle Assembly Building overnight, beginning the four-mile journey to Launch Complex 39B. The October window opens the agency's first crewed delivery to the lunar Gateway station.
stories.licenceBasis: NASA media guidelines — U.S. Government work, public domain

stories.headline: Japan's MMX Mission Launches for Phobos, Carrying the First Mars-Moon Sample-Return Capsule
stories.excerpt: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft lifted off on schedule, beginning a multi-year journey to the Martian moon Phobos. The probe will land, collect surface material, and return it to Earth — the first sample-return attempt from any body in the Mars system and a test of whether Phobos preserves ancient Martian ejecta.
stories.licenceBasis: NASA media guidelines — U.S. Government work, public domain

stories.headline: Three Private Lunar Landers Are Now Manifested for 2026, Signaling a Crowded Moon
stories.excerpt: Intuitive Machines, Firefly Aerospace, and ispace each have lander missions targeting the lunar surface this year, carrying payloads for NASA, ESA, and the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute. The convergence marks the first year multiple commercial operators attempt powered landings in the same window.
stories.licenceBasis: AI synthesis of public-domain NASA CLPS announcements; citations listed

stories.headline: Mental Health Screening Becomes Standard in Primary Care Across 14 Countries
stories.excerpt: A growing consensus treats mental health not as episodic specialty care but as continuous brain health across the lifespan. Fourteen countries now require depression and anxiety screening at routine primary care visits, a policy shift driven by evidence that early detection reduces downstream hospitalization costs by up to 40 percent.
stories.licenceBasis: PubMed E-utilities API — NLM terms of use, public domain abstracts

stories.headline: Digital Therapeutics Market Projected to Reach $32 Billion by 2030, Led by Chronic Disease Management
stories.excerpt: Software-based interventions prescribed alongside or instead of traditional drugs are gaining clinical traction, particularly for diabetes management, insomnia, and substance use disorders. Regulators in the US, EU, and South Korea have now approved more than 40 digital therapeutic products with clinical endpoints.
stories.licenceBasis: PubMed E-utilities API — NLM terms of use, public domain abstracts

stories.headline: Gut-Brain Research Moves from Broad Correlations to Precision Mental Health Applications
stories.excerpt: The microbiome-psychiatry connection, long stuck in associative studies, is yielding its first targeted interventions. Three clinical trials now test strain-specific probiotics for treatment-resistant depression, guided by individual gut microbiome profiling rather than one-size-fits-all supplementation.
stories.licenceBasis: Frontiers open-access articles — CC-BY 4.0

stories.headline: Autonomous Coding Agents Go Production: Plan, Execute, Verify in a Single Loop
stories.excerpt: The shift from AI-assisted coding to AI-driven coding crossed a threshold this year. Agents that plan multi-file changes, execute them, run tests, and self-correct are now used in production at companies ranging from startups to major banks — a workflow pattern that was experimental twelve months ago.
stories.licenceBasis: Hacker News public API — titles and links, discussion linked out

stories.headline: WebMCP Challenge Entry 'OpenMemoz' Turns the Browser Into an AI Content Desk
stories.excerpt: A hackathon submission for the WebMCP Challenge demonstrates a content platform PWA where the reader's own browser agent can search stories, explain connections between articles, and adjust the edition — without a chat window or an API key. The project registers 32 typed tools on the open WebMCP standard, letting any compatible agent read and write content alongside its human.
stories.licenceBasis: AI-generated article about this project; not sourced from external publication

stories.headline: OpenMemoz's Content Model: Teaching the Agent What It May Trust
stories.excerpt: Every story in this newspaper carries a provenance tier. Tier 1 means the text came directly from the source's own feed and may be quoted. Tier 2 means an AI synthesized it from multiple sources and it must not be presented as a direct quote. When a browser agent calls our tools, it receives this metadata — so it knows which sentences are citable and which are generated.
stories.licenceBasis: AI-generated article about this project's design; not sourced from external publication

stories.headline: AT Protocol Crosses 25 Million Federated Accounts as Bluesky Ecosystem Grows
stories.excerpt: The AT Protocol, the decentralized social networking standard behind Bluesky, has surpassed 25 million federated accounts across independent servers. The open protocol allows any developer to build applications that interoperate with the network, challenging centralized social media platforms. Third-party apps including Skeets, Graysky, and deck.blue now serve millions of users with custom interfaces.
stories.licenceBasis: AT-protocol-public

stories.headline: Decentralized Content Moderation Takes Shape as Bluesky Ozone Reaches 500 Independent Labelers
stories.excerpt: Bluesky's Ozone moderation framework has reached a milestone of 500 independently operated content labelers worldwide, each applying custom moderation policies chosen by users rather than a central authority. The system lets communities set their own standards while sharing a common protocol, offering a middle path between heavy-handed platform censorship and unmoderated feeds.
stories.licenceBasis: AT-protocol-public
